A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bayesian-LoRA. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original commonsense reasoning, WikiText-2, MATH, distribution-shift, efficiency, and ablation results, with additional analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Qwen3-14B and Llama-3.1-8B experiments, AIME evaluation, and configuration-stability studies. Table 20 separately attributes the TFB comparator results to prior work.

M1.justification: The inducing-variable model, normalizing flow, stochastic LoRA-factor sampling, training objective, and inference modes remain. Matching Algorithm 1 across its relocation shows the same computational procedure; corrected distribution labels and matrix dimensions repair its mathematical description rather than introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds AIME 1983–2023 training data and AIME 2024 evaluation within the existing mathematical-reasoning domain. Commonsense, WikiText-2, MATH, and MMLU coverage remains. Additional backbones on retained datasets are configuration changes rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with LoRA+ and AdaLoRA on Qwen3-14B classification tasks, C-LoRA on six Llama-2-7B benchmarks, and BLoB-Mean + TFB on Llama-3.1-8B (Tables 17, 19–20). The original main-table comparator sets remain. TFB scores are explicitly imported from the cited work.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen3-14B and Llama-3.1-8B configurations, historical AIME training with a 30-problem 2024 test set, and controlled adapter-placement and inducing-shape sweeps. The Monte Carlo analysis reverses the reported ARC/OBQA ID/OOD assignments. Tables 11 and 14 revise sampling settings and selected BO hyperparameters; these corrections do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds studies of seed stability, adapter placement, and symmetric versus asymmetric inducing matrices on ARC-Easy (Tables 21–23). Existing flow-depth, rank, MAP-recovery, and Monte Carlo analyses remain, with revised flow-depth findings and ID/OOD interpretation. Table 15 also removes two BO candidate entries.

E5.justification: v2 already reports means and standard deviations over three seeds. v3 adds a separate five-seed Qwen3-14B study, naming the seeds and reporting individual outcomes plus mean and standard deviation (Table 21). This does not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 17–23 add substantial results. For example, AIME accuracy is 80.0% for both LoRA and Bayesian-LoRA, with ECE 11.26 versus 5.26. Existing values also change: Table 5's one-flow-layer NLL changes from 0.57±0.12 to 0.49±0.02, Table 6's OBQA MAP ECE changes from 16.1±0.6 to 9.80±1.0, and BO records are revised.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the inducing-location matrix dimensions and explicitly separates prior covariance ΣW from variational covariance λ²ΣW. Appendix A adds a joint-KL chain-rule derivation explaining the conditional penalty. These are localized mathematical repairs; the principal propositions and final ELBO form remain.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the contribution from a closed-form ELBO independent of weight dimensionality to an ELBO with a closed-form conditional KL term. The central probabilistic-LoRA, deterministic-limit, efficiency, and calibration claims remain. Tasks newly mentioned in the abstract were already covered elsewhere in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning shared function families, structured uncertainty versus noise injection, selective prediction and routing, and stability across configurations. It revises the flow-depth explanation to describe one-layer NLL as near-optimal. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix K claims the lowest average ECE despite Table 1 giving Laplace a lower mean. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and NVIDIA H100 hardware disclosure. It clarifies task-specific sampling budgets, fixed main-comparison hyperparameters versus separate BO analysis, and settings for the added configuration studies. Most existing preprocessing, optimizer, inducing-model, and MATH training details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Uni-LoRA, C-LoRA, and TFB citations and positions the latter two as complementary contextual and post-hoc approaches. Section 2 removes BLoB from its characterization of full-model Bayesian inference. The principal SGP/LoRA positioning remains; the flow-process reference's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits the abstract and explanatory passages, standardizes terminology and sampling notation, and adds acknowledgements and affiliation text. The OOD analysis becomes a separate appendix and new appendices extend the existing structure. The main narrative organization and much of the prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven result tables and two accuracy–ECE plots, moves Algorithm 1 into the main text, and reformats main result tables. The existing Pareto plots are substantially enlarged and relocated. v2's Monte Carlo sensitivity figure is removed while its numerical tables remain; Figures 1–2 retain their graphics with revised captions.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through clearer prior/variational distinctions, a narrower closed-form claim, corrected numerical reporting, code/hardware disclosures, and targeted comparison and robustness evidence. These benefits provide a limited net improvement. New claims about downstream decision quality remain untested, and Appendix K incorrectly claims the lowest average ECE: Table 1 gives Laplace approximately 4.82 versus Bayesian-LoRA's 5.03.
